passage: Sunday night, before the move. Amandeep and I finally had The Talk, by video, with tea on both sides. We had been guessing what the other expected, so I asked: "What do you actually need from me?" Amandeep said a quick message every day, even a boring one. And honesty about feelings, even when it is awkward. I said I need room during exams and I will not be able to talk much some weeks. We wrote it in a shared note under the heading "our rules, subject to change". Five lines. Amandeep added: "If one of us goes quiet, we ask, not assume." I feel lighter, like a knot loosened a little. Tomorrow I go. Not scared, just aware. — Kamal

qa.q: What heading did Kamal and Amandeep write on their note?
qa.a: They wrote the heading 'our rules, subject to change'.

qa.q: What is Kamal feeling at the end of the entry?
qa.a: Kamal feels lighter and calm, describing a knot that loosened a little, and aware rather than scared about the move.

qa.q: What alternative approach could the couple add after some months, and why?
qa.a: They could review the note together every few months, because needs change and a review keeps the rules from turning into old promises.

qa.q: How might Amandeep see the talk?
qa.a: Amandeep asks for a daily message and honesty and adds the rule about asking, so Amandeep seems to want closeness and clarity more than long calls.

grounding: Shows a couple discussing what each needs before a move and writing shared expectations, with a place for exam time.

passage:
Alka: ok before I leave on sunday. you said we should talk about what we each need. go first
Sharmila: fine. I need one message a day. not an essay. just 'alive, ate, tired'
Alka: easy. mine: if something's bothering you, say it. don't go quiet and make me guess
Sharmila: that's fair. I do that 😅
Sharmila: and in december I have finals. I'll need space. not because I care less
Alka: noted. then in march it's my turn, thesis deadline
Sharmila: so what do we write down?
Alka: 1. one message a day minimum. 2. say feelings out loud, even small ones. 3. exam months = less talking, no sulking
Sharmila: 4. we read this list again at new year
Alka: pinning it 📌
Sharmila: ok. I feel better now. still going to miss you ❤️

qa.q: What does Sharmila say one daily message can be?
qa.a: Not an essay, just 'alive, ate, tired'.

qa.q: Why does Sharmila add 'not because I care less' about December?
qa.a: Sharmila is worried Alka might feel hurt or pushed away by less contact, so Sharmila explains in advance that the space is about finals, not feelings.

qa.q: What else could the pair add to their list?
qa.a: A way to handle a missed day, like one short voice note, so a slip does not become a guessing game.

qa.q: How might Alka feel reading 'I feel better now'?
qa.a: Alka is likely relieved too, since the talk turned vague worries into a pinned list they both agreed to.

grounding: Shows a couple before a move talking through what each needs, a daily message, honesty and space in exam months, and writing a shared list.

passage:
On the bench outside Farhan's tea stall near the Sinnar bus stand, Ojas and Gauri had an hour before his bus to Bengaluru. Farhan brought two cutting chais and quietly went back to his stove.
'Let's not just say "we'll manage",' Gauri said. 'What do you actually need from me?'
Ojas thought about it, turning the glass. 'To hear from you every day. Even one line. When I don't hear anything, my head starts making stories.'
'I can do that. I need you to tell me when you're upset, not act normal and go cold.' She took a small notebook from her bag. 'And in April, my nursing exams. I'll go quiet for two weeks. That's not about us.'
He nodded. Together they wrote three lines, one message a day, say what hurts, exam weeks are protected, and each photographed the page.
The bus horn sounded. Farhan waved from the stall as it pulled out.

qa.q: Where were Ojas and Gauri sitting before the bus?
qa.a: On the bench outside Farhan's tea stall near the Sinnar bus stand.

qa.q: What does Ojas mean by 'my head starts making stories', and what feeling is behind it?
qa.a: He gets anxious when there is silence and imagines something is wrong, so one line a day would reassure him.

qa.q: What could Ojas and Gauri do if one of the three lines stops working?
qa.a: Agree on a time, say after the April exams, to reread the page together and change it.

qa.q: How might the plan look to Gauri during her April exams?
qa.a: Gauri can study without guilt, since they already agreed her quiet weeks are not about the relationship.

grounding: Shows a couple before a move naming what each needs, a daily line, honesty about hurt and exam space, and writing it down together.
